reading.body:
Google operates a facility in Hocking Township as part of a multi-county data center campus in the New Albany and Columbus area of Ohio. The company does not publish power capacity, square footage, or building-level specifications for individual facilities, disclosing only aggregate investment figures at the state level. The Fairfield County site sits within a $1.7 billion regional investment that Google announced alongside new capacity in Lancaster, positioning it alongside AWS and Meta as a major hyperscale operator in the same corridor.

The facility cannot be assessed for its contribution to AI infrastructure without published power or rack specifications. Ohio has 76 mapped data center facilities, but only eight publish power figures, totaling 60.4 MW of disclosed capacity across the state. This facility is not among the eight, so no ranking of its size relative to published Ohio capacity is possible.

Google's non-disclosure of building-level specifications is consistent across its portfolio and reflects a deliberate policy rather than a data gap. For readers tracking which campuses matter to AI scaling, this site can confirm Google operates here and that the broader regional investment is substantial, but cannot translate those facts into compute density or grid demand without access to specifications the operator has chosen not to publish.
